questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transport in the region was less expensive than expected. Every first weekend of the month regional trains in Occitanie only cost 1€.  With these trains, you can go as far as to Toulouse among many other destination. The tickets are quickly sold out, but it is always possible to use the app Fairtiq to benefit from the 1€ tickets the first weekend of the month. This app works a bit similar to the rejsekort system, where you check in when you board the train, and you check out when you get off the train.
The regional busses (liO bus) are always 1€ and can bring you to many different destinations. To see the schedule, download the liO app.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your traineeship destination (city/region)? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The university of Perpignan offers many sports courses etc. They are for free for Erasmus students, so no excuse not to sign up!

Get the pass' culture! Is is free for erasmus students and gives you discounts on plenty of cultural activities, including theatre, concerts, cinema, rugby matches etc.

I used it a lot to get cinema tickets for the cinéma castillet in the city centre for 3€! I also enjoyed going to concerts in Archipel and to see rugby matches of the local rugby club USAP.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with locals? *
questions.answer: Socializing with locals can be challenging, since they of course already have an established social circle and do not necessarily "need" the contact with international students visiting only for a few months. But it is not impossible. Participating in the many cultural activities that the university offers at Maison des Sports or Maison des Art et de la culture (MAC)  is a good starters to get to know local students. Then there are also many oportunities to volunteer in the Perpignan, for example in MIAM, a associative vegan restaurant that offers lunch for very affordable prices.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Bad weather, even if for Danish standards, the weather could be considered "good" is a valid reason here not to show up to a meeting with friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going on a traineeship to the same city/region? *
questions.answer:
Housing: A room in the student accodmodation is much cheaper than alternatives on the free market, but also much smaller. So it is great for saving money that you then can spend on other things than rent, but you also will have to live in a small room. So think about what is the most important to you.
Duration of the stay: One semester is good, but it takes time to get used to the place and to explore the region. So consider staying for the academic year.
Perpignan itself: The city can seem underwhelming at first, due to its size and apparent lack of activities. But don't be fooled, there are more activities than one might think! First of all, the region around the city is stunning. Perpignan is located between the Pyrenees and the Mediterranean Sea with a beautiful coast line! So no matter if you want to hike in the mountains, or by the rocky coast, go to the beach, or do any other kind of outdoor activity, Perpignan and its region has you covered! And within the city, you have lots of small concert places, like Nautilus, théâtre de complicité, archipel etc etc. I wrote a list with things to explore under the next question.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future traineeship students? *
questions.answer:
This is a non exhaustive list with general recommendations for activitie and places to visit that I have for future exchange students: (I structured the list on the platform, but on the report, all this structure is lost, so I hope you can still read it)

Things to do in Perpignan and its surroundings:

In Perpignan itself

Get the pass'culture.
	-> It is for free for exchange students and gives you discounts many different kinds of activities (cinema, theatre, concert, rugby matches etc.). You get it in "la boutique" on the campus moulin à vent, where you also buy your tickets for the different events. 

Palace of the Kings of Majorca, 
Sports Park for running, 
Bar Hakem Park, 
Le Grabuge (bar in Perpignan)
	-> small, alternative bar with kitchen, where the owner makes her own beer and bread. The atmosphere is super nice they often have different events an exhibitions. THe owner is super nice and always ready for a chat!, 

The Nautilus
	-> cultural centre with many concerts and other activities such as pub quizzes, debates etc. People here are also generally very nice and super open minded. 

MIAM
 -> associative vegan restaurant/café mainly driven by volunteers. You pay 5€ for the yearly subscription and then you can eat lunch there every day for a price you determine yourself. The food is really good and they also have different kinds of activities in the evening, such as language cafés, debates, theatre spectacles. It is also a good place to involved as a volunteer yourself. 

Rugby match of USAP with the pass'culture,                               

immediate surroudnings of Perpignan (reachable within 1 hour):

coastal trail (sentier du littoral)
-> The sentier du littoral is a hiking path along the beautiful coastline in the region. The cities on the sentier du littoral are easily accesible by the regional train. In it's entirety, it is 30km, but there are several villages on the way, where you can end your hike to take the train or bus back to Perpigan. Between some of the cities (e.g. between Collioure and Argelès sur mer) the hike does not take longer than 1.5 h. Cities to visit on the sentier du littoral:  

Banyuls, 
Portbou, 
Cerbère, 
Collioure and the fort —> coastal trail (sentier du littoral) towards Argelès-sur-Mer,                        


Other destination in the immediate surroundings of Perpignan      

Ille-sur-Têt with the "orgues" formations (not on Sunday), 
Villefranche de Conflent with Fort Liberia or hiking, 
Salses Fortress, 
Céret, 
The Yellow Train in Villefranche,                          


Nearby(ish) cities in the region easily accesibly with the monthly 1€ tickets:

Montpellier, 
Toulouse, 
Nîmes, 
Avignon, 
Carcassonne, 
Narbonne and Narbo Via                       


Nearby cities in Spain
Girona, 
Barcelona                                                  



With a car:
Serrabona, 
Canigou, 
Andorra, 
Saint Cyprien (feasible by bus but complicated), 
vallée heureuse , 
Canyoning, 
Figueres, 
Cadaqués                                      

General advice:
Use Fairtiq to save money on train tickets, 
LIO buses for 1-2€, 
First weekend of the month (buy in advance, or use Fairtiq) tickets in the whole region are for 1€, 
Pass’culture: cheaper tickets for cinema, theater, and rugby, 
Free sports courses (website of SUAPS UPVD), 
Do not go to Luna in Canet, 
Take advantage of the salle de culture générale  in the university library, 
Ouigo for cheaper TGV, even in Spain
